---
title: "Week 6: The Stories Clinical Data Won't Tell You"
---

## Theme: NLP and Injury Surveillance: Reading the Invisible

Structured data --- ICD codes, admission diagnoses --- systematically
misses the context of injury. A woman admitted for \'facial trauma\' may
be a survivor of intimate partner violence; a child coded for
\'accidental fall\' may have been pushed. This week we use natural
language processing to extract hidden injury mechanisms from ED
narratives and introduce the CourtListener API for scraping and
analyzing public health caselaw.

**Assignment 2 Check-In:** Assignment 2 is due Friday Feb 27 --- one

ACEs); (2) identified at least two datasets from the course data catalog

## Classroom Lab Demonstration

**Legal Focus:** Burden of proof and narrative evidence in civil
litigation; how text-based data extraction is used to establish patterns
of systematic harm; the Free Law Project and public access to federal
court decisions via CourtListener (courtlistener.com).

**Health Focus:** The gap between structured ICD-coded injury data and
the actual mechanisms of harm recorded in clinical narratives; intimate
partner violence as a systematically undercoded diagnosis; natural
language processing as an injury surveillance tool.

**Data:** NEISS (National Electronic Injury Surveillance System)
narrative data subset (provided on Carmen, from
cpsc.gov/Research\--Statistics/NEISS-Injury-Data); CourtListener federal
court decision API (courtlistener.com/help/api); CDC NVDRS narrative
excerpts (Carmen, IRB-approved subset).

**R Code:** tidytext::unnest_tokens() for tokenization;
tidytext::bind_tf_idf() for TF-IDF analysis; stringr::str_detect() and
regex patterns for mechanism extraction; httr::GET() and
jsonlite::fromJSON() for CourtListener API calls; ggplot2 for frequency
bar charts and timeline plots.

- Load NEISS narrative data subset from Carmen; use tidytext to tokenize
  narratives and compute TF-IDF by injury type and sex

- Extract mechanism categories (Object, Action, Location) using regex
  and keyword dictionaries provided on Carmen

- CourtListener lab: make httr::GET() API calls to search for federal
  IPV + housing cases; download case metadata (court, date, docket
  number); produce a timeline of caselaw by federal circuit

- Optional: pass 20 anonymized ED narratives to an LLM API for mechanism
  classification; compare output to regex results
